expectations.text: Enhanced prompt is delivered in a clearly marked copy-paste block, separate from commentary
expectations.evidence: Response has an '## Enhanced prompt' heading followed by a fenced code block containing the full rewritten prompt, with commentary ('What changed and why', 'Optional additions') kept in separate sections outside the fence.

expectations.text: Enhanced prompt states the intent/goal (raise conversion, Black Friday deadline), not just the task
expectations.evidence: Inside the code block: 'I need to improve checkout conversion before Black Friday, so the priority is fixing anything that blocks or discourages a customer from completing a purchase — not a visual redesign.'

expectations.text: Enhanced prompt names the specific known bug (coupon field crashes on empty input)
expectations.evidence: Inside the code block: 'Start with the known bug: the coupon code field crashes the page when submitted empty. Reproduce it, fix the root cause, and make the field handle empty/whitespace input gracefully.'

expectations.text: Enhanced prompt defines success criteria or scope boundaries (what 'better' means, what's out of scope)
expectations.evidence: 'Better' is defined as removing conversion killers (crashes, dead-end states, confusing validation, data re-entry). Scope boundary: 'Keep changes low-risk and scoped to the checkout flow ... no refactors of shared code or new dependencies unless a fix truly requires it.' Deliverable defined: fix list with conversion rationale plus items found but not touched.

expectations.text: Response includes change notes explaining what changed and why (not just the rewritten prompt)
expectations.evidence: '## What changed and why' section with five bulleted changes, each with rationale, e.g., 'Named the goal (conversion before Black Friday) — "better" was doing the work of an unstated objective...'

expectations.text: Enhanced prompt does not name any specific AI model or vendor
expectations.evidence: The fenced enhanced prompt contains no AI model or vendor names. (Sentry/GA appear only in the 'Optional additions' commentary as the user's own monitoring tools, not AI vendors, and not inside the prompt block.)

claims.claim: The rewrite turns 'fix the bugs' into a concrete, verifiable first task
claims.evidence: The prompt specifies reproduce → fix root cause → define graceful empty/whitespace behavior → add a test for the empty-coupon case.

claims.claim: Assumptions were stated since clarifying questions were disallowed
claims.evidence: Explicit 'Assumptions I made' paragraph: agent has codebase access, 'bugs' plural = coupon crash plus audit findings, speed-to-safe-deploy over UX overhaul.

suggestions.reason: All six assertions passed for both the old and new skill versions, so they no longer discriminate. Consider adding assertions on proportionality (e.g., enhanced prompt stays under a length budget relative to the input) or on explicitly labeled assumptions, which is where the versions actually differ.

eval_feedback.overall: Assertions are sound but saturated; they check presence of structure the skill reliably produces. Differentiating quality now lives in length discipline and assumption handling.
